Q1: Pentachlorobenzene exhibits known significant hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), oral hazards (ORL), and organ and systemic hazards (OGN). It also shows expanded concern for endocrine disruption (EDC2). However, data regarding inhalation (IHL) and dermal/eye (SKN) hazards are currently deficient (Tier 4), warranting a precautionary approach.
Q2: Pentachlorobenzene is recognized on "Lists of Concern" as a potential endocrine disruptor by the TEDX list. Furthermore, it is identified as a Persistent Organic Pollutant, underscoring its significant environmental persistence and hazard.
Q3: Pentachlorobenzene is relatively well-characterized, evidenced by a substantial number of scientific references (3995), a specific molecular formula (C6HCl5), and its classification as a well-defined "Small Molecule." Despite this general depth of study, there are specific data deficiencies regarding its inhalation and dermal/eye hazards.
